segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics digest from November 1st, 2026.
Today we cover the latest on humanoid development, AI error recovery, and exciting new robot welcomes.
Tune in for the updates.
From Humanoids Daily, Meta reportedly built a humanoid prototype named Max with Fourier, and work on a second version is currently in progress.
The development focused on creating an internal humanoid research unit utilizing advanced computing for human interaction studies.
Max measures approximately one point five meters in height and weighs around forty-eight kilograms, and it operates using NVIDIA Jetson Thor computing.
The development concentrated on advanced human interaction capabilities, including voice recognition and gesture interpretation.
Meta indicated that this collaboration is for internal research and experimentation, with no intention to market the units.
Future work on the Max two iteration involves planned redesigns and the integration of additional sensors.
This development signals ongoing internal exploration in advanced physical robotics and sophisticated human-machine interface technologies.
From Humanoids Daily, Rhoda AI Shows Robots Recovering From Factory Edge Cases in Schrep Visit.
This report details a demonstration where robots successfully recovered from factory edge cases, including accidental grasps and retrieving trapped items during unpacking.
The system employs video prediction to guide robot actions, which are then translated into movement commands by a separate inverse dynamics model.
Tasks were learned efficiently utilizing only ten to twenty hours of teleoperation data subsequent to extensive video pre-training.
The company has stated an objective to achieve paid production deployments for wheeled industrial robots before the end of 2026.
This research highlights successful recovery within specific tasks, while sustained factory reliability remains an area for future development.
Industry focus will likely remain on the advancement of reliable real-world deployment for these robotic systems.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, eHand-6!".

This report details the introduction of the eHand 6, an affordable industrial robotic hand from Hitbot, which is positioned as an accessible option in the industrial dexterous hand market with noted performance specifications.
The eHand 6 was introduced in May 2025 with a price point of four hundred twenty dollars.

Manufactured by Hitbot and integrated within the Xiaomi ecosystem, the device exhibits technical ratings indicating low scores for Degrees of Freedom at two out of five and Strength at one out of five, suggesting a developing system.
Prospective buyers are advised to consider the trade-off between the low cost and these modest performance specifications.
The development of such accessible robotic hardware signals continued exploration in the industrial automation sector.
And that's all the circuits for today!
From building 'Max' to decoding the future, keep those algorithms humming.
Thanks for plugging into the world of robotics.
Until tomorrow, keep innovating!
